problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{2}.$ 
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to S}$ from $B$ to $S$ if 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Change-of-Coordinates Matrix When One of the Bases is the Standard Basis

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ is

examples.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ consists of the vectors $\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2,$ and $\mathbf e_3,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065461/assets/0d9a23830f48d4659dd963110d9322c12e8d4849bd9bcd63ae9d5adb0e1fba05.png)

The components of the vectors in $\mathcal{B}$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065461/assets/10b5f2e35da56c7be6d547827164c68f475df4d012116b9666c12a94bbc39f55.png)

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{S}.$ 

Therefore, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065461/assets/06ef110e61fcdf044e15300d50bc5ac918b37e8351c1aa6b77124dd2029c9aa3.png)

Finally, $a=0,$ $b=0,$ and $c=10.$

feedback.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}-{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{2} & =5{c}_{3}+2{c}_{2}, \\ {b}_{3} & ={c}_{2}-{c}_{1},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ a & b & 1 \\ -1 & c & 0\end{aligned}]?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $c=5.$
